{{Short description|French-American mathematician}}
'''Philippe Di Francesco''' is a French-American mathematician, focusing in mathematical physics, physical combinatorics and integrable systems. He is senior researcher (Directeur de Recherche) at the [[Institute of Theoretical Physics, Saclay]] in France, and is currently the Morris and Gertrude Fine Distinguished Professor of Mathematics at [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philippe Di Francesco |url=http://www.math.illinois.edu/~philippe/ |access-date=May 13, 2017 |publisher=illinois.edu |archive-date=July 20, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170720134544/http://www.math.illinois.edu/~philippe/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Philippe Di Francesco |url=http://physics.illinois.edu/people/directory/profile/philippe |access-date=May 13, 2017 |publisher=illinois.edu}}</ref> He is also author of the book 'Conformal Field Theory'.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9780387947853 |title=Conformal Field Theory |publisher=Springer |year=1997 |isbn=978-1-4612-7475-9 |series=Graduate Texts in Contemporary Physics |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-2256-9}}</ref> He received his PhD in 1989, under Jean-Claude Le Guillou and [[Jean-Bernard Zuber]], at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philippe Di Francesco |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=265689 |website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

Di Francesco was elected as member of [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.
